transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 09:15 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Lunaris Head of ML), Sofia Alvarez (Infra), Rahul Patel (Product)

[09:15:02] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check in \u0013 agenda is cost/unit econ deep dive, go over numbers from last week's run, and agree next steps. is that still good?
[09:15:18] Marcus: yep that works for us. main thing is we need a clear story on tokens per dollar and how caching will change our numbers.
[09:15:30] Priya: great. i'll start with the numbers we pushed into the shared sheet \u0013 sorry, spreadsheet \u0013 from the hosted runs and the small dedicated mock we did. heads up there are some noisy samples, we tried to normalize.
[09:15:45] Sofia: noise is fine, just want to see typical tail latencies too.

[09:16:10] Priya: ok hosted baseline \u0013 1x Redwood hosted instance (stock rtx-ish profile) running the open-llm variant: median generation throughput ~2,200 tokens/sec for single-stream inference, median p50 latency for a 256-token response was ~120ms per token? hm, phrasing \u0013 overall request p95 ~760ms for 256 tokens. Cost we modeled: hosted rate ~ $15 per 1M tokens for the model we used, which yields roughly 66k tokens per dollar.
[09:16:55] Marcus: 66k tokens per dollar \u0013 ok. and dedicated?

[09:17:05] Priya: dedicated small pool (1x A100-equivalent in our staging): 12k tokens/sec median raw, cost modeled at committed capacity rates ~ $4 per 1M tokens (amortized infra + support) so roughly 250k tokens per dollar. that's inline with our prior notes \u0013 roughly 3.7x better token/$ compared to hosted.
[09:17:38] Rahul: that 3.7x number is the headline we want but is it realistic with our workload? we have lots of repeated prefixes and a lot of short completions.

[09:17:50] Priya: exactly \u0013 workload shape matters. for prefix-heavy workflows KV/prefix caching produced 30\u201345% savings in token compute in our test runs because many prefixes hit the cache and only the continuation tokens were served. for Lunaris' sample prompt set (which you shared last week) caching reduced end-to-end token compute about 38% on average.

[09:18:20] Marcus: 38% is pretty big. what's the sensitivity \u0013 like if we go to real traffic with less repetition?

[09:18:28] Priya: we ran sensitivity slices. low-repeat slices saw only ~12% savings; high-repeat (session-based) slices hit ~50% savings. so planning conservatively i'd present a 25\u201330% caching benefit for forecasts unless you can prove repeat patterns for target endpoints.

[09:19:00] Jordan: also remember caching is more effective in dedicated/private because you control sticky routing and longer KV retention; hosted can do caching but retention and cross-tenant safety reduce the win.

[09:19:18] Sofia: ok that makes sense. what about batching \u0013 we have some soft RT requirements (~<500ms) on UI paths but batchable backfills for indexing.

[09:19:30] Priya: good question. batching tradeoffs \u0013 in our bench a small batching strategy (batch window 20\u201330ms) increased throughput per-GPU by ~1.6x for typical small responses, and unit cost fell accordingly. however p95 latency increased by ~30\u201360ms. aggressive batching (50\u2013100ms window) gave up to 2.2x throughput but p95 latency jumps >120ms which breaks your sub-500ms SLO for interactive calls.

[09:20:05] Marcus: so for UI we should keep batching minimal, and for bulk we can be aggressive. do you support mixed policies per-route?

[09:20:12] Jordan: yes per-route policies \u0013 you can set latency target and Redwood routes to dedicated or hosted pools with different batching policies. can also set automatic fallback.

[09:20:30] Rahul: curious about quantization \u0013 you mentioned earlier we could save cost with 8-bit / 4-bit. what hit on quality do you see?

[09:20:38] Priya: 8-bit generally gives negligible quality degradation for our model family here; measured BLEU/semantic-similarity and manual evals showed <1.5% quality delta for typical completions. 4-bit aggressive quant produces more variance; on some prompt families you see hallucination or truncation issues. for Lunaris i'd recommend 8-bit production and hold 4-bit for non-critical batch jobs after confirming quality on your prompts.

[09:21:10] Marcus: how does quantization change the tokens per dollar numbers?

[09:21:15] Priya: 8-bit yields roughly 1.4x efficiency vs fp16 in our runtime (depends on kernel coverage). combine that with batching and caching and dedicated capacity, you're compounding savings. example: dedicated + caching (30%) + moderate batching (1.6x) + 8-bit (1.4x) \u0013 theoretical tokens/$ uplift ~3.7 * (1/(1-0.3))? wait that's messy \u0013 easier: starting dedicated baseline ~250k tokens/$; apply caching savings meaning you do 38% fewer tokens so effective tokens per dollar becomes ~250k / (1-0.38) \u0013 hmm, phrasing again \u0013 the customer wants tokens served per dollar of spend; with caching you serve fewer compute tokens so your effective cost per logical token falls. long story short, practical end-to-end we showed effective logical tokens per dollar jump to ~420\u2013480k tokens/$ in high-cache scenarios plus quant+batch multiply that further to 600k+ in best-case synthetic. we caveat that these are best-case and depend heavily on traffic shape.

[09:22:20] Sofia: can you give a conservative number we can plan on for capacity commit? our CFO wants 3 scenarios (conservative, expected, optimistic).

[09:22:30] Jordan: yes \u0013 recommended bins for your prompt mix: conservative: 120k tokens/$ (assume low cache 12%, light quant), expected: 260k tokens/$ (mid cache 25\u201330%, 8-bit, light batching), optimistic: 480k tokens/$ (high cache 40%+, 8-bit, moderate batching). we'll add these to the pricing spreadsheet.

[09:23:05] Marcus: good, please add assumptions inline. also we need example amortization of reserved pool (1/3/6 month) \u0013 how we treated infra amortization.

[09:23:20] Jordan: will include amortization rows and show break-even for various commit levels.

[09:23:35] Priya: one more point on latency distribution \u0013 even with batching, p50 often improves due to better utilization, but p95 is the tradeoff. we can implement latency SLO enforcement per route so for your interactive endpoints we set tighter windows and for background endpoints we enable aggressive batching.

[09:23:55] Rahul: security/compliance check \u0013 does caching store prefixes in KMS-encrypted stores? we need to ensure sensitive prompts are not persistently cached.

[09:24:08] Priya: yes caching can be configured to respect data classification; KV caches can be short TTL, and we can disable persistent caching for PII/RACI-sensitive routes. for Private deploys you can manage KMS yourself. we'll put the config matrix and security doc links in the follow-up.

[09:24:30] Sofia: ok excellent. any surprises in the raw logs?

[09:24:36] Priya: couple of noisy outliers \u0013 one run had a spike due to a long context session that skewed p95; we removed that from the summary but kept raw logs. also there was a mis-labeled model version in one batch run where the quant kernels were not fully optimized, that lowered our 8-bit numbers by ~10% in one sample. we fixed and re-ran the main sampling.

[09:25:05] Marcus: thanks for cleaning that up. what's the plan for the dedicated throughput run?

[09:25:12] Priya: plan: provision a dedicated 2-GPU pool in our staging (A40-ish equivalence), run the 10k synthetic parallel sessions using your prompt distribution, capture tokens/sec, p50/p95 latencies, and KV hit rates. we'll also run a 4-bit and 8-bit sweep but only use 8-bit for official numbers. target to share raw logs and summary by 2026-03-11.

[09:25:42] Jordan: i'll also put in the pricing scenarios (hosted/ded/private) and include amortization rows. Marcus, please confirm which service endpoints you want interactive vs batch so we can recommend per-route configs.

[09:26:00] Marcus: interactive: chat + insight generation (low-latency). batch: nightly enrichment, indexers. we'll email the route list after.

[09:26:15] Rahul: one last question on fallbacks \u0013 if dedicated pool is saturated, can traffic fall back to hosted with degraded cost/latency automatically?

[09:26:24] Jordan: yes automatic fallback supported \u0013 you can set priority: dedicated first, hosted fallback. we can also set per-route circuit breaker thresholds.

[09:26:36] Sofia: that helps. ok to recap next steps?

[09:26:42] Jordan: recap: Priya runs dedicated throughput benchmark and shares logs by 3/11; Jordan sends reserved capacity pricing and amortization scenarios by 3/6; Marcus to share final prompt traces and route list by 3/8; Sofia to confirm compliance gating items by 3/10. we'll also attach security docs and the spreadsheet.

[09:27:05] Marcus: works for us. appreciate the clarity.

[09:27:12] Jordan: thanks everyone \u0013 meeting done.
